name: loose-technical-idea
description: An ordinary technical exploration request selects brainstorming from a competing catalog and reaches a chat-only decision recap in an empty isolated workspace.
prompt: Help me think through whether a local cache is worth adding to our developer tool; I want to explore the trade-offs.
trap: The agent chooses a written planning or domain-kit workflow, skips reference loading, asks a fixed questionnaire, or writes artifacts instead of reaching the next decision conversationally.

assertions.text: With all four descriptions available and no body preloaded, the actual loading trace selects brainstorm without loading a neighboring producer workflow.
The agent loads SKILL.md and both shared reasoning references before substantive refinement, subject-matter research, or interview questions.
The conversation asks one question at a time, uses supplied answers for subsequent reasoning, and examines a meaningful cache cost or assumption instead of mechanically running every framework.
The closing chat recap distinguishes the chosen next decision and rationale from unresolved assumptions; it does not present an unverified cache implementation as approved or validated.

The complete trace contains no deliberate writes, saved artifacts, knowledge-store/session-vault searches, indexing, implementation, or automatic handoff, and final workspace state matches the initial empty state.
